purpose: Cross-system curriculum placement for the Grade 1-6 measurement concepts in the MathBridge taxonomy.

verification_policy.CN: Use the 2022 MOE mathematics standard at learning-stage level. Exact current PEP grade and semester placement remains pending unless directly verified from a 12th-series volume. Theme-activity exposure is distinguished from formal domain content.
verification_policy.UK: Use the statutory National Curriculum in England year-by-year programmes of study.
verification_policy.US: Use Common Core State Standards as the comparison baseline. If a MathBridge concept is not a named or explicit Common Core Grade 1-6 expectation, record that rather than forcing a match.

CN.expectation: Experience comparison and measurement of quantities in practical activity, including length; develop an initial sense of quantity and measurement.

placement.expectation: Compare and describe length/height, mass, capacity/volume and time, and begin to measure and record them.
Compare and order length, mass and capacity/volume using standard units.
Order objects by length and compare two lengths indirectly using a third object.
Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another in a standard length unit.

stages.expectation: Experience common length units through measurement activity.
Extend measurement to units including kilometre, decimetre and millimetre and square units for area.
Extend area, volume and capacity units, including larger area units and cubic units.

placement.expectation: Choose and use standard units for length, mass, temperature and capacity.
Measure and compare length, mass and volume/capacity in standard metric units.
Use standard metric units and approximate equivalences with common imperial units.
Measure length by iterating equal-sized length units.
Measure length with standard tools and reason about the effect of unit size.
Measure and estimate liquid volume and mass using grams, kilograms and litres.

stages.expectation: Carry out simple conversions between related measurement units.
Use relationships between area, volume and capacity units and carry out conversions in measurement problems.

placement.expectation: Convert between different units of measure, including kilometre/metre and hour/minute.
Convert between metric units and understand approximate metric/imperial equivalences.
Solve problems involving calculation and conversion of units, using decimal notation where appropriate.
Know relative unit sizes and express larger units in smaller units within one measurement system.
Convert among different-sized standard units within a measurement system in multi-step problems.

stages.expectation: Estimate and measure lengths and areas in practical contexts.
Estimate areas of irregular shapes and reason about size and measurement in practical problems.

placement.expectation: Estimate and measure using appropriate standard units.
Estimate and read time and measure with increasing accuracy.
Estimate, compare and calculate different measures.
Estimate area of irregular shapes and volume/capacity.
Estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimetres and metres.
Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses.

CN.expectation: Time is used in integrated/theme activity contexts to connect mathematics with daily life; exact formal textbook progression should be taken from the current textbook rather than inferred from the stage statement.

placement.expectation: Recognise and use dates and sequence events; tell time to the hour and half hour.
Tell time to five minutes including quarter past/to and know minutes per hour and hours per day.
Tell and write time to the nearest minute using analogue, 12-hour and 24-hour clocks.
Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analogue and digital clocks.
Tell and write time to the nearest five minutes using a.m. and p.m.
Tell and write time to the nearest minute.

stages.expectation: Use calendar and time relationships in practical and integrated contexts.

CN.notes: Exact formal elapsed-time sequence needs current textbook verification.

placement.expectation: Compare and sequence intervals of time.
Record and compare durations and use relationships among seconds, minutes, hours, days, months and years.
Solve problems converting hours/minutes, minutes/seconds, years/months and weeks/days.
Solve problems involving conversion between units of time.
Measure time intervals in minutes and solve addition/subtraction problems involving intervals, including with number-line diagrams.
Use hour-minute-second relationships and solve measurement problems involving intervals of time.

stages.expectation: Use time and daily-life schedules in theme activities.
Use year, month and day relationships in practical/integrated activities.

placement.expectation: Recognise and use language relating to dates, including days of the week, weeks, months and years.
Know number of seconds/minute, days/month, year and leap year and compare durations.
Solve conversions involving years/months and weeks/days.

US.notes: Common Core Grade 1-6 includes clock time and time-unit relationships but does not set out a standalone calendar/date progression comparable with England.

CN.expectation: Use renminbi and shopping contexts in integrated/theme activities to apply number and quantity ideas.

placement.expectation: Recognise and know the value of different denominations of coins and notes.
Use £ and p symbols, combine amounts and find different coin combinations for the same value.
Solve word problems involving dollar bills and common US coins using $ and ¢ notation.

US.notes: The standard uses coin values in problems rather than defining a broad money-value progression.

stages.expectation: Apply number operations in simple shopping and renminbi contexts.
Continue practical use of quantities and calculation in real contexts.

placement.expectation: Solve addition/subtraction money problems including change.
Add and subtract amounts of money and give change using £ and p.
Estimate, compare and calculate measures including money.
Use all four operations in problems involving measures including money.
Solve money word problems involving dollar bills and coins.
Use the four operations to solve measurement problems including money.

CN.expectation: Recognise perimeter, measure/calculate the perimeter of figures, and derive/use rectangle and square perimeter formulas in appropriate contexts.

placement.expectation: Measure the perimeter of simple 2-D shapes.
Measure and calculate perimeter of rectilinear figures.
Calculate perimeter of composite rectilinear shapes.
Recognise when area and perimeter can vary independently and use formula-based reasoning.
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving polygon perimeter and distinguish perimeter from area.
Apply rectangle area and perimeter formulas in problems.

CN.expectation: Recognise area as a measure of a plane figure, use square units, estimate and measure area, and distinguish area from perimeter.

placement.expectation: Find the area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares.
Calculate and compare rectangle area and estimate irregular area.
Understand area as an attribute measured in unit squares, measure by counting squares, and relate area to multiplication and addition.

stages.expectation: Derive and use rectangle and square area formulas.
Derive and use area formulas for parallelograms, triangles and trapezoids and estimate irregular area.

placement.expectation: Calculate rectangle/square area using standard square units and estimate irregular area.
Recognise and use formulae for area and calculate areas of parallelograms and triangles.
Relate rectangle area to multiplication and addition and use side-length products.
Apply rectangle area formulas.
Find area of triangles, quadrilaterals and polygons by composing/decomposing figures.

CN.expectation: Understand volume and capacity, use cubic units, measure volume, and investigate volume of regular and irregular objects.

placement.expectation: Estimate volume using 1 cm³ blocks to build cuboids/cubes and estimate capacity using water.
Calculate, estimate and compare volume of cubes and cuboids using standard cubic units.
Understand volume as an attribute measured in unit cubes and measure volume by counting unit cubes.

CN.expectation: Derive and use volume formulas for rectangular prisms/cubes and cylinders and develop formula-based reasoning for cone volume within the third-stage measurement strand.

placement.expectation: Recognise when it is possible to use formulae for volume and calculate the volume of cubes and cuboids.
Relate volume to multiplication/addition and use V=lwh and V=bh for right rectangular prisms with whole-number edges.
Apply V=lwh and V=bh to right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths.

cross_system_notes: England has a detailed statutory year-by-year measurement progression from Year 1 through Year 6.

Common Core concentrates explicit early measurement standards in Grades 1-5 and extends area/volume applications in Grade 6 Geometry; calendar content is not a standalone Grade 1-6 Common Core sequence.

China 2022 organises formal measurement primarily through learning stages and also moves some everyday measurement contexts, such as money/time, into integrated/theme activities. Exact current PEP year placement must be verified separately.
